content: 1. Patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers and are taking seladelpar in combination with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors should avoid this combination. Alternative therapies are recommended. 2. Grapefruit consumption increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, resume the original selumetinib dose. Monitor closely. 3. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of sertraline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of sildenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. 6. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of simvastatin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. 7. Avoid consuming large quantities of grapefruit or grapefruit juice (e.g., more than 1 quart per day) as it increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. Coadministration of siponimod with both moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and moderate/strong CYP2C9 inhibitors is not recommended. 8. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. 9. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of solifenacin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of sonidegib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 11. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of sorafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Grapefruit and sparsentan may increase each other's toxicity through pharmacodynamic synergy. Avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, interrupt sparsentan treatment and consider dose titration when resuming. 13. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of sufentanil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase sufentanil plasma concentrations, leading to prolonged or severe adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression. 14. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of sulbactam/durlobactam by mechanisms involving OATP1 inhibition, which may increase sulbactam plasma concentrations. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. Monitor closely. 15. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of sunitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of suvorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. Suvorexant is not recommended with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 17. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of tacrolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of tadalafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of talazoparib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. Talazoparib is a P-gp substrate, and coadministration with P-gp inhibitors may increase systemic exposure. 20. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of tamoxifen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, which decreases its conversion to the active metabolite N-desmethyl tamoxifen. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of tamsulosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Dose reduction may be necessary for coadministered drugs predominantly metabolized by CYP3A. 22. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. 23. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of temsirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of teniposide by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of terbinafine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of tezacaftor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. Avoid foods containing grapefruit or Seville oranges. 27. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of theophylline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of ticagrelor by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of tinidazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of tipranavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of tisotumab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Its active metabolite (MMAE) is a CYP3A4 substrate, and coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase systemic exposure and adverse effects. 32. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of tofacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. No specific dose adjustment is recommended with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, but reduce the dose if coadministered with both moderate CYP3A4 and potent CYP2C19 inhibitors. 33. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of tolterodine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. 35. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of trabectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., less than 14 days), administer it one week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it the day before the next infusion. 36. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of trazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of triazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of vadadustat by mechanisms involving OAT1/OAT3 inhibition, which may increase vadadustat AUC. Monitor closely for rapid or excessive hemoglobin response and adverse reactions. 40. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of valbenazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the dose to 40 mg once daily when coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 41. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of vamorolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the starting dose to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day if weight is over 50 kg. 42. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of vandetanib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 43. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of vardenafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of vemurafenib by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (P-gp) efflux transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of venetoclax by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The use of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated during the initial ramp-up dosing phase. Avoid grapefruit products, Seville oranges, and starfruit during treatment. 46. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of verapamil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of vinblastine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 48. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of vincristine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 49. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of vincristine liposomal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 50. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of vinorelbine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 51. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of voclosporin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. The use of grapefruit is contraindicated. 52. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of zaleplon by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 53. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of zanubrutinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid grapefruit or use an alternative drug. 54. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of ziprasidone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 55. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of zolpidem by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 56. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of zonisamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 57. Grapefruit increases the levels or effects of zuranolone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Reduce the dose if coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 58. Avoid excessive consumption of grapefruit during pregnancy and lactation. Controlled studies in pregnant women show no evidence of fetal risk.
